identity.title: Normalizing Flows are Capable Generative Models

problem.claim: The work asks how capable normalizing flows can be as likelihood-based generative models for continuous inputs.

gap.claim: Despite promising prior results, normalizing flows had received relatively little recent attention, and their power was believed to be underestimated.

contributions.claim: TarFlow, a simple scalable Transformer-based normalizing-flow architecture, stacks autoregressive Transformer blocks over image patches with alternating directions.
Three sample-quality techniques are proposed: Gaussian-noise augmentation, post-training denoising, and guidance for conditional and unconditional generation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present TarFlow as enabling highly performant normalizing-flow models and report stand-alone normalizing-flow generation with diffusion-comparable quality and diversity for the first time.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that TarFlow achieves new state-of-the-art image likelihood-estimation results, exceeding previous best methods by a large margin.
The authors report sample quality and diversity comparable to diffusion models, using a stand-alone normalizing-flow model.

narrative_sequence.summary: Normalizing flows are likelihood-based models for continuous inputs and have shown promise, but recently received limited attention.
The authors introduce TarFlow, a Transformer-style masked autoregressive flow over image patches with alternating autoregressive directions.
They add noise augmentation, denoising, and guidance techniques to improve generated-sample quality.
They report leading image likelihood results and diffusion-comparable sample quality and diversity, alongside a code release.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns an architectural description with separate techniques for sample quality, then connects the combined system to distinct likelihood and generation outcomes.

lessons.interpretation: Separating core architecture from targeted quality interventions can make a multi-objective contribution easier to attribute.
lessons.application: For a generative-model paper, describe the base model, each quality intervention, and the specific metric or capability each is intended to improve.
lessons.exception: This structure is less suitable when interventions cannot be meaningfully isolated or when the work presents only one indivisible mechanism.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, likelihood metrics, numerical margins, or evaluation protocols.
The basis and scope of the reported comparison with diffusion models are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the claimed state-of-the-art or first-time status.
